text: The native NAD phosphorylation and dephosphorylation pathway contains three core transformations: ATP-dependent NAD phosphorylation, NADP hydrolysis, and proton-coupled transhydrogenation. The E. coli evidence supports individual activities and condition-dependent nucleotide balancing, but does not identify the physiological cytosolic NADP phosphatase or establish a complete cycle in every strain. The broader native taxonomic range is curated pathway scope, not a measurement of flux in every listed organism. Soluble SthA is included as an opposing supporting redox activity, outside the three native member reactions.
independent_assessments: Native XML has precisely the three named members. SthA is clearly marked as supporting chemistry, and the Escherichia coli record does not claim universal flux across the native pathway's broad taxa.
The native hypothetical NADP phosphatase has neither a gene nor an exact UniProt bridge. The record retains the unknown physiological activity and the authors' negative CysQ interpretation.
Fresh Rhea11693 and issuing SthA chemistry support NAD+NADPH to NADH+NADP without proton transport. It is clearly a supporting opposed redox route outside the native three-member boundary.

text: The exact directional reactions are RHEA:18630, NAD(1−)+ATP(4−)→NADP(3−)+ADP(3−)+H+; RHEA:28051, NADP(3−)+water→NAD(1−)+hydrogenphosphate(2−); and RHEA:47994, NADH(2−)+NADP(3−)+H+(outside)→NAD(1−)+NADPH(4−)+H+(inside). Each side has coefficient one. The two proton appearances are distinct transport sides and are not canceled. RHEA:11693 describes the supporting soluble NAD(1−)+NADPH(4−)→NADH(2−)+NADP(3−) reaction without proton transport. Compartments remain explicit in the source participants and edge descriptions; one shared proton chemical identity does not erase the transport.
independent_assessments: Fresh Rhea participant/compound traversal and elemental/charge accounting support all five NadK sides. ATP is the core donor and NAD oxidation state is preserved.
Fresh Rhea hydrolysis sides consume water and produce hydrogenphosphate. Neither the reaction identity nor native unassigned activity identifies a physiological cytosolic enzyme.
Fresh Rhea 47994 is the selected reverse direction of its master. Its six sides preserve outside and inside proton participants even though both use the same chemical CURIE.
Fresh Rhea11693 and issuing SthA chemistry support NAD+NADPH to NADH+NADP without proton transport. It is clearly a supporting opposed redox route outside the native three-member boundary.

text: Frozen PathBank SMP0002093/PW002081 corroborates the three-event boundary: two BiochemicalReaction objects plus one TransportWithBiochemicalReaction. Its class-specific count of two does not mean that the transport event is absent. Its NAD, NADH, NADP, NADPH, ATP, ADP and phosphate references use CHEBI:15846,16908,18009,16474,15422,16761 and18367, respectively, rather than all of the exact Rhea charge forms. Those forms are not asserted to be exact chemical matches. The frozen diagram also assigns both transport protons to the same Inner_Membrane entity; it supplies structural context, not inside/outside topology or physical membrane localization of the nucleotide pools.
independent_assessments: The original OWL contains two BiochemicalReaction instances plus one TransportWithBiochemicalReaction attached to the pathway. Counting only the first class was not the biological boundary; the final prose corrects it.
The original PathBank event uses the same Inner_Membrane entity for both protons. Final prose treats it as a coarse representation; physiological orientation is established independently.
Frozen PathBank acid/base forms and its structural references were read independently of Rhea. The final record does not claim exact equivalence between the differing charge forms.

text: NadK is a homohexamer in the native assembly and the 2001 purification, approximately180 kDa with approximately30-kDa subunits. The native assembly object CPLX0-682 has no direct name, so its display remains unnamed while its six-chain NadK interpretation is stated here. Endogenous MG1655 protein was purified3400-fold after growth at37°C for18 h. Its measured N terminus MDNHFKCIGI differs at residue2 from the deduced/current reference MNNHFKCIGI. The separately expressed pSK67 yfjB construct used pET14b NcoI/BamHI in BL21(DE3)pLysS, with empty SK45 as control; the vector name alone does not establish a retained His tag. The reference NadK is cytoplasmic by reviewed rule-based annotation, with an annotated proton-accepting residue73; the historical preparations are not assigned that exact sequence merely by accession.
independent_assessments: Native component coefficient six and the 2001 approximately 180/30-kDa measurements agree. The unnamed native object is retained without inventing a direct name; adapter acceptance is separate from science.
The measured MDNHFKCIGI and reference MNNHFKCIGI differ at position two. Native purification and recombinant construct qualifiers preserve this rather than claiming identical sequences.
The original cloning and host passages support pSK67 in pET14b/BL21(DE3)pLysS and SK45 control. No retained tag is inferred merely from vector choice.

text: The 2001 purified-NadK assay used5 mM NAD and ATP,5 mM MgCl2,100 mM Tris at pH7.0 and37°C. At5 mM donor, reported relative activities were ATP100%, UTP109%, CTP60%, GTP56%, dATP42% and TTP40%. These alternate in-vitro donors do not redefine the native ATP core. Polyphosphate at1 mg/mL and the tested pyrophosphate, tripolyphosphate, trimetaphosphate, hexametaphosphate, metaphosphate, ADP, AMP, phosphoenolpyruvate, phosphocreatine, glucose6-phosphate and p-nitrophenylphosphate did not support the measured phosphorylation. NADH, ADP-ribose, adenosine, AMP, ADP and ATP were not phosphorylated as acceptors in experiments described as data not shown. Activity peaked near pH7.5 and60°C;65°C for10 min removed about half the activity.
independent_assessments: Fresh Rhea participant/compound traversal and elemental/charge accounting support all five NadK sides. ATP is the core donor and NAD oxidation state is preserved.
The original donor table supports 100/109/60/56/42/40 percent for ATP/UTP/CTP/GTP/dATP/TTP at the stated concentration. These alternatives are narrative assay scope, not extra core chemistry.

The original donor table includes polyphosphate variants and negative small donors. The final paragraph preserves tested conditions, including metaphosphate/hexametaphosphate, without converting absence into inhibitor edges.

text: Replacing the divalent metal at1 mM gave relative NadK activities Mg100%, Mn242%, Zn104%, Ca85% and Co73%. FeCl2, CuCl2, NaCl, KCl, LiCl and no-metal conditions gave no detected activity in that replacement experiment. Failure to substitute for Mg is not inhibition of an Mg-containing assay. The supported metals are alternatives, not a claim that all occupy the hexamer simultaneously or that the fastest in-vitro metal is physiologically preferred.
independent_assessments: The replacement-metal table supports Mg/Mn/Zn/Ca/Co at 1 mM. Metal-support edges are alternative assay cofactors, not a claim of simultaneous occupancy.
FeCl2 establishes Fe(II), now CHEBI:29033. Copper and monovalent chloride substitutions and metal omission failed to support activity; none is misrepresented as inhibition of a Mg-containing assay.

text: The 1987 NadK preparation came from an unspecified E. coli K12 substrain grown in forced-aerated glycerol minimal medium at37°C and harvested in late log phase. It was enriched93-fold and was explicitly not homogeneous. In the assay with10 mM NAD and ATP,14 mM Mg and100 mM MOPS pH7.2, NADPH at5–30 µM strongly inhibited activity, while NADH at50–200 µM was roughly tenfold weaker. Their effects were additive. NAD saturation became sigmoidal, with reported Hill coefficients1.8–2.1 for NADPH and1.7–2.0 for NADH; increasing NAD could overcome inhibition. These kinetic observations and native allosteric annotations do not locate a binding site experimentally. The abstract assigns Km1.9 mM to NAD and2.1 mM to ATP, whereas the Results reverse those assignments; both are retained as an internal discrepancy.
independent_assessments: Original 1987 rate curves and the 2001 table support NADH/NADPH negative effects. Native allosteric signs agree; the 93-fold partially purified K12 preparation is explicitly distinct from the later MG1655 protein.
The original abstract and Results swap the 1.9/2.1 mM NAD/ATP assignment. The record preserves the discrepancy instead of selecting one as an uncontested value.

text: In the 2001 preparation, NADPH at5 and10 µM left58% and24% activity, while NADH left68% and39%. NADP at50 and100 µM left83% and79%, contrasting with the absence of a significant NADP effect in the 1987 conditions. Quinolinate, nicotinate, nicotinamide, nicotinamide mononucleotide, ADP and AMP likewise had no significant effect in the earlier experiment. Varying adenylate energy charge from0 to1 at4 mM total adenylates, with or without15 µM NADPH, did not change the 1987 rate. Those negative findings are condition-limited and do not imply that adenylate composition never influences nucleotide metabolism.
independent_assessments: Original 1987 rate curves and the 2001 table support NADH/NADPH negative effects. Native allosteric signs agree; the 93-fold partially purified K12 preparation is explicitly distinct from the later MG1655 protein.

Both studies support the described difference, but nad-041 currently assigns the 1987 comparison solely to a 2001 table locator. Issue 466 requires a separately owned PMID3025169 Table2/adjacent-text citation; the inhibition direction under 2001 conditions is valid.
The 1987 adenylate-charge experiment uses fixed total adenylates with and without NADPH. Its negative result does not contradict later SthA activation, a different enzyme and assay.

text: The 2001 NadK thiol-reagent experiment used a glucose6-phosphate dehydrogenase reporter instead of the inhibitor-sensitive isocitrate dehydrogenase reporter. DTT,2-mercaptoethanol and glutathione at1 mM left100% activity. PCMB at1,0.25 and0.1 mM gave no detected activity,33% and51%; HgCl2 gave no detected activity,35% and54%. HgCl2 remains the salt, not a free-mercury node. The unspecified PCMB salt/charge is retained as reagent prose rather than forced onto an acid or anion identity. Table3 reports its own kcat values55/125 and efficiencies22/38; these are not silently recalculated from another table. Failed recovery of a yfjB disruption, described as data not shown, suggested essentiality under those conditions rather than proving universal essentiality.
independent_assessments: The original cloning and host passages support pSK67 in pET14b/BL21(DE3)pLysS and SK45 control. No retained tag is inferred merely from vector choice.

The 2001 thiol reagent table and adjacent method specify reporter substitution because of sensitivity. HgCl2 is an exact reagent node; PCMB and unchanged reducing agents remain properly bounded prose.

text: The 2005 primary abstract and issuing NadK variant annotations distinguish R175G/H/Q/T, which gain NADH-kinase activity, from R175E/I/K, which do not. R175G also lowers the NAD-kinase Vmax. These variants are not assigned to the wild-type endpoint and do not contradict the negative wild-type acceptor assay. The full 2005 body was unavailable.
independent_assessments: Exact issuing R175 mutagenesis features and the available 2005 abstract support gain-of-NADH-kinase variants. Wild-type NADH phosphorylation and unavailable full preparation details are not inferred.

text: The native physiological NADP-phosphatase object has no assigned gene. Purified alkaline phosphatase converted historical TPN to DPN in the 1962 source, supporting in-vitro NADP hydrolysis. That paper used GL, BAP, PV and HH preparations with AMP-based specific activities1230,1130,1130 and1060 units/mg, but the TPN sentence identifies neither a particular fraction nor an E. coli strain. Its standard assayA contained0.05 M Tris pH8.2,0.01 M substrate and0.2–1 enzyme units in0.5 mL for20 min at37°C; assayB used p-nitrophenylphosphate at4×10−4 M. No exact reference sequence, processing isozyme or particular fraction is retrospectively assigned to the TPN observation.
independent_assessments: The complete retained 1962 transcription explicitly states TPN-to-DPN conversion. It does not identify which of four preparations supplied that particular observation, and the record avoids inventing one.
The native hypothetical NADP phosphatase has neither a gene nor an exact UniProt bridge. The record retains the unknown physiological activity and the authors' negative CysQ interpretation.

text: Reviewed PhoA is periplasmic, with a1–21 signal peptide and a mature reference chain beginning at22. Its Ser124 annotation describes the phosphoserine catalytic intermediate. The reference binds two Zn ions and one Mg ion per subunit; these are per-chain capacities, not three coefficient-one ions assigned indiscriminately to a whole dimer. Isozymes1 and3 have identical-chain dimers, whereas isozyme2 combines the differently processed chains. DsbA-assisted folding and Iap-related N-terminal processing are protein-maturation context, not evidence for NADP-specific regulation. The native report of additional phosphite oxidation is a separate PhoA function, not another NADP-core reaction. Periplasmic localization and the native enzyme record’s physiological-relevance flag do not establish a cytosolic recycling loop.
independent_assessments: Issuing PhoA location, signal peptide and mature-chain features support periplasmic processing. This evidence does not support a physiological cytosolic NADP loop.
Issuing PhoA cofactor annotation specifies two Zn and one Mg per chain. Edge endpoints and prose keep per-chain capacity separate from the native dimer and historical metal occupancy.
The native hypothetical NADP phosphatase has neither a gene nor an exact UniProt bridge. The record retains the unknown physiological activity and the authors' negative CysQ interpretation.
Reviewed PhoA signal/chain/PTM comments support processing and isozymes. DsbA/Iap context and native phosphite oxidation are not presented as NADP-specific regulation or core reactions.

text: The 1962 PhoA inhibitor/activation observations largely concern p-nitrophenylphosphate or AMP, not NADP. They include strong cadmium inhibition, urea effects that depend on exposure time and can reverse, and substrate/salt-dependent stimulation; the text reports activating fluoride and p-hydroxymercuribenzoate conditions and more modest mercury/cobalt effects. Competitive phosphate inhibition is discussed with prior-work attribution. Mg plus phosphate can protect against heat inactivation, while concentrated NaCl can worsen it; KCl can block recovery and fluoride, urea or CuSO4 can slow recovery in their stated experiments. The flattened primary-table rendering does not justify invented precise row/column values, and none of these broad-substrate or renaturation results is relabeled a direct inhibition measurement of NADP turnover.
independent_assessments: The 1962 paper's metal, heat, urea and polyamine results concern broad-substrate pNPP/AMP experiments. No NADP-specific causal edges are inferred from them.

text: The 2007 CysQ preparation was the GFP-free ASKA AG1 pCA24N construct, carrying N-terminal His6 plus TDPALRA and C-terminal GLCGR extensions. At37°C, pH8.0 and10 mM MgCl2 it hydrolyzed NADP and NADPH. Reported Km and kcat were2.70±0.53 mM and0.70±0.09 s−1 for NADP, and2.13±0.25 mM and1.45±0.18 s−1 for NADPH. The additional NADPH substrate activity is retained as assay context, not an extra member of the three-event core. PAP preference and the different optima led the authors to conclude that CysQ probably is not the physiological E. coli NADP phosphatase.
independent_assessments: The 2007 Methods identify AG1 ASKA, GFP removal and both terminal extensions. The final qualifier preserves a tagged recombinant preparation rather than pretending it is an exact native chain.
The 2007 Table2 and adjacent results support in-vitro NADP/NADPH hydrolysis at pH8, 37C, 10mM Mg. The extra NADPH substrate is not promoted into the three-member core.

The study's substrate preferences and low-Mg/pH limitations explicitly oppose physiological NADPase assignment. Current reference localization and general calcium inhibition do not override that conclusion.

text: CysQ NADP(H)ase activity was undetectable at pH6.4 or0.2 mM Mg, conditions more favorable to its PAPase. Matched Fbp and SuhB extracts were negative controls;15 mM NaCl,7.5 mM imidazole and2.5% glycerol carried with the preparation did not explain the activity. LiCl IC50 values were70 mM for NADP,60 mM for NADPH,10 mM for FBP,0.05 mM for3-PAP and0.15 mM for2-PAP; table dashes mean not determined. Reviewed CysQ calcium/lithium inhibition from the separate 2006 nucleotidase study is general protein context, not a calcium experiment on the 2007 NADP assay. Its annotated peripheral inner-membrane location is on the cytoplasmic side and still does not resolve the physiological catalyst.
independent_assessments: The near-physiological pH/low-Mg failures, SuhB/Fbp negative controls and buffer controls are preserved. These bounds materially weaken a physiological NADPase assignment without denying other CysQ activity.

The visually checked lithium table gives 70/60/10/0.05/0.15 mM for the five substrates. Dashes mean not determined, and the edge uses the LiCl reagent rather than an unqualified elemental lithium node.

The study's substrate preferences and low-Mg/pH limitations explicitly oppose physiological NADPase assignment. Current reference localization and general calcium inhibition do not override that conclusion.

text: The 2007 archaeal comparisons used MJ0109, AF2372 and MJ0917 constructs in separately specified BL21/OrigamiB expression contexts and assays at85°C with20 mM Mg, pH8.5. Their activities are not assigned to E. coli CysQ or to one physiological E. coli loop. A later paper’s estimate of approximately140 NADP molecules dephosphorylated per cell per second is a citation to older work, not a firsthand reconstruction of that experiment. The 1971/1973 primary bodies and abstracts were unavailable; their bibliographic records and native/later-paper framing remain explicitly secondary evidence for the historical turnover claim.
independent_assessments: The archaeal enzymes and 85C assays are separate comparative contexts. The paper's starred/undetermined measurements are not transferred to E. coli.
The1971/1973 historical metabolism papers are metadata-only in the inspected corpus. The record explicitly avoids inventing first-hand assays from those inaccessible papers.

text: PntAB is a dimer of heterodimers: two PntA and two PntB chains in the native complex. The UniProt heterodimer description denotes the protomer and does not conflict with the α2β2 assembly. Its cytoplasmic nucleotide-binding domains dI and dIII handle NAD(H) and NADP(H), while membrane domain dII couples them to proton movement; FAD is not assigned as a Pnt cofactor. Native historical annotation gives AB (Re–Si) specificity, transferring the pro-R hydrogen of NADH and pro-S hydrogen of NADPH; this is not a new stereochemical measurement in the 2021 experiment. The 2021 pSA2-derived pET16b construct was expressed in THO C43(DE3) Δcyo ΔpntAB with an alpha N-terminal His6 tag and thrombin site. Tag cleavage was not reported. DDM-purified protein and proteoliposomes represent distinct preparations.
independent_assessments: Native coefficients are two alpha plus two beta; the 2021 dimer-of-heterodimers model agrees. A UniProt heterodimer describes the protomer and does not contradict the assembly.

Issue 465 is corrected in c2fec: location-comment assertions are narrowed, own topological features support cytoplasmic domains, and the primary introduction/Figure1 citation is explicitly a homology model.
The primary 2021 construct and purification passages identify alpha His6/thrombin-site PntAB and the THO deletion host. No unreported cleavage or native liposome orientation is asserted.

text: The 2021 natural forward NADH/NADP and reverse NADPH/NAD assays used their stated regenerating systems; APAD-dependent reverse and cyclic assays were separate. The cyclic reaction does not carry net proton transport. Reported apparent Km values were NADPH4.1±1.2 µM, NAD108±12 µM, NADP37±7 µM and NADH6.8±1 µM. The source gives fixed NADH as50 µM in Methods but500 µM in Results; those descriptions are not silently reconciled. Reconstitution incorporated65±10% protein, with approximately75±5% of reverse-active and85±5% of cyclic-active sites facing outward. These are proteoliposome orientation estimates, not an inversion of cellular topology.
independent_assessments: Issue 465 is corrected in c2fec: location-comment assertions are narrowed, own topological features support cytoplasmic domains, and the primary introduction/Figure1 citation is explicitly a homology model.
The primary 2021 construct and purification passages identify alpha His6/thrombin-site PntAB and the THO deletion host. No unreported cleavage or native liposome orientation is asserted.
APAD reverse/cyclic assays and orientation measurements are distinguished from natural forward transfer. The Methods/Results 50-versus-500-uM NADH inconsistency remains visible.

text: Reverse Pnt hydride transfer generated a proton gradient and supported a co-reconstituted ATP synthase. The βH91A variant, no-enzyme controls and ionophores tested the coupling; ATP synthesis belongs to the separate ATP synthase, not the Pnt stoichiometry. An ATPase-generated proton motive force stimulated NADPH formation7±1.8-fold without ionophore,6.4±0.8-fold with valinomycin, and1.6±0.3-fold with CCCP plus valinomycin. The proposed gated-channel and dIII-flip mechanisms are mechanistic interpretations. Thermus thermophilus structural models and prior domain experiments do not become an experimental E. coli full-complex structure.
independent_assessments: H91A, no-enzyme and ionophore controls support coupled proton transport. ATP production belongs to co-reconstituted ATP synthase, not a PntAB substrate/product edge.
The forward natural-nucleotide reconstitution experiment shows pmf stimulation under those conditions. Reported fold effects and ionophore controls remain assay-specific, not universal cellular flux.

text: Older Pnt inhibitor papers were available as primary abstracts and native annotations. DCCD inhibits transhydrogenation and proton pumping; NADH protects, while NADP and, less strongly, NADPH accelerate inhibition. In the 1993 αD232/E238/E240 mutant series, the proteins retained40–90% activity and proton pumping, while triple substitutions reduced DCCD sensitivity. Those historical residues/preparations are distinct from the 2021 βH91A construct. NBD chloride modifies βC147/260 and other residues; NADPH protects some domain modification, but an NBD–NADPH reaction product is itself strongly inhibitory. The adduct has no invented exact chemical identity here.
independent_assessments: Native negative regulation and available older primary abstracts support DCCD/NBD inhibition. The record accurately says older full bodies and full construct details were inaccessible.
Older DCCD abstracts retain nucleotide-dependent protection, charged-residue mutants and preserved pumping. They are not conflated with the2021 H91A coupling mutant.

The NBD abstract includes beta cysteine and other modification sites and the inhibitory NBD-NADPH adduct. The record avoids a simplistic universal NADPH-protection claim and leaves unresolved adduct chemistry in prose.

text: The 1999 Pnt topology abstract used cysteine-free, His-tagged single-cysteine variants in intact cells and inside-out membranes, supporting four alpha and nine beta membrane spans in that experimental model. Native comments also preserve older nucleotide-affinity, cysteine-free and βD213 contexts. These are source-specific topology and kinetic studies, not measurements on the 2021 preparation. Reference-chain residue numbering, domain models, tags and assay directions remain distinct.
independent_assessments: Issue 465 is corrected in c2fec: location-comment assertions are narrowed, own topological features support cytoplasmic domains, and the primary introduction/Figure1 citation is explicitly a homology model.

The NBD abstract includes beta cysteine and other modification sites and the inhibitory NBD-NADPH adduct. The record avoids a simplistic universal NADPH-protection claim and leaves unresolved adduct chemistry in prose.

text: Soluble SthA, also called UdhA, is represented as an octamer with reference P27306. The 1999 cloning abstract corrected an N-terminal genome-sequencing error; its older7–8-subunit interpretation is retained alongside the exact native octamer and the later approximately440-kDa SEC/DLS estimate. The 2022 K12 sthA construct carried a C-terminal His10 tag in pBXC3H and was expressed in MC1061; FAD was added during lysis before affinity and SEC purification. Reviewed capacity is one FAD per subunit, whereas a native historical comment reports measured occupancy0.76 mol FAD/subunit. Partial FAD loss during SEC is preparation-dependent. Native B-stereospecificity is explicitly not experimentally determined.
independent_assessments: Native octamer and 2022 SEC/DLS estimates agree at assembly level. Older seven-to-eight-subunit annotation and other-species filament observations remain separate.
The primary 2022 construct is His10-tagged SthA in MC1061, with FAD in lysis. It is distinct from the older fused protein and the AlphaFold structure identifier.

FAD occupancy, SEC loss and lower variant activity are supported by primary results and supplements. Native per-chain capacity is not universal occupancy, and mutant findings stay out of wild-type edges.
The1999 abstract/native annotation supports a corrected N terminus and soluble enzyme identity. Modern issuing sequence grounding is independent; no unavailable full paper is credited.

text: The 2022 kinetic assay followed NADH/thioNADP transhydrogenation, opposite to the supporting physiological NADPH-to-NAD reaction. ThioNADP is a surrogate, not NADP. At5 mM, AMP, ADP and ATP raised wild-type activity to160.7±2.9%,171.1±7.2% and148.2±8.9%. Corresponding C45A values were454.9%,991.8% and363.1%; T50C values were222.9%,319.2% and177.4%. Each series uses its own no-adenylate baseline:8.66±0.83,0.55±0.10 and0.92±0.18 µmol/min/mg for wild type, C45A and T50C. Large mutant percentages therefore do not imply higher absolute mutant activity or restore the wild-type mechanism.
independent_assessments: The 2022 kinetic donor/acceptor pair is NADH/thioNADP; the 2004 extract capacity uses APAD. Neither surrogate is silently made natural NADP/NAD or a new native pathway substrate.

FAD occupancy, SEC loss and lower variant activity are supported by primary results and supplements. Native per-chain capacity is not universal occupancy, and mutant findings stay out of wild-type edges.
The original supplement gives WT responses160.7/171.1/148.2 percent at5mM, on its own baseline. Large C45A/T50C percentages use much smaller separate baselines and are not assigned to WT.

text: Sodium and potassium phosphate inhibited the 2022 SthA surrogate assay, approaching residual activities of approximately20–25% and15% around50 mM. NaCl/KCl controls showed no significant change through50 mM, but500 mM left approximately70% and40%; high ionic strength is not universally inert. The hydrogenphosphate reference node denotes phosphate-buffer chemistry, not isolation of one protonation species. NADH above7 mM gave substrate inhibition with KI12.1±2.0 mM at0.5 mM thioNADP; thioNADP itself had KI0.59±0.26 mM. Neither observation establishes inhibition by natural NADP under all conditions.
independent_assessments: Phosphate inhibition and Na/K chloride controls are concentration-dependent. Low-salt absence of an effect is not generalized to500mM, and buffer phosphate protonation is not directly measured.
High NADH inhibits the thioNADP assay with the stated concentration range and fitted KI. The older NADPH-direction observation and unresolved thioNADP chemical identity remain separate.

text: SthA can also oxidize NADH or NADPH with oxygen in uncoupled assays, releasing predominantly hydrogen peroxide with some superoxide. No-enzyme blanks and anaerobic persistence of reduced flavin constrain that interpretation. The wild-type coupled assay partitioned approximately98% to thioNADPH and2% to ROS; C45A gave62.3% hydride-transfer and37.1% peroxide-associated partitioning, while T50C gave89.2% and10.2%, at much lower total transfer rates. Reported flavin-reduction k_red/Kd were303±50 s−1/88±27 µM for wild type,710±160/300±100 for C45A and2200±400/227±61 for T50C. These mutant and side-activity observations do not add an oxygen-consuming core reaction or establish a universal cellular ROS flux.
independent_assessments: FAD occupancy, SEC loss and lower variant activity are supported by primary results and supplements. Native per-chain capacity is not universal occupancy, and mutant findings stay out of wild-type edges.

Primary uncoupled oxidase/oxygen experiments support side activity and ROS, with mutant relative versus absolute yields distinguished. These are not added as native core reactions or proven cellular ROS flux.

text: The 2022 paper distinguishes the reference P27306 sequence from AlphaFold model AF-B7M718-F1 and modeling with Thermus thermophilus lipoamide dehydrogenase2EQ7; these are not an experimental structure of the exact reference chain. A12-nucleotide sthA/oxyR overlap motivated a redox-stress hypothesis but did not demonstrate an OxyR→sthA regulatory edge.
independent_assessments: The 12-base overlap motivates an OxyR hypothesis only. The record has no invented OxyR regulatory edge.
The paper's reference sequence and AF-B7M718-F1 model are not the same identity claim. No experimentally determined reference-protein crystal structure is asserted.

text: The 2011 purified fused-EcSTH primary abstract describes NADPH/thio-NAD activity, Km68.29 and133.2 µM, optimum35°C and pH7.5, stimulation by adenylates at2 mM, and inhibition by Mn, Co, Zn, Ni and Cu. After30 min preincubation, strong inhibition persisted only for Zn, Ni and Cu. Full Methods and the exact fusion sequence were unavailable. Its description of excess-NADPH product inhibition is preserved as the source’s terminology even though NADPH is the named assay substrate; it is not converted into a different reaction direction. These abstract-level results do not replace the 2022 salt controls or wild-type His10 preparation.
independent_assessments: High NADH inhibits the thioNADP assay with the stated concentration range and fitted KI. The older NADPH-direction observation and unresolved thioNADP chemical identity remain separate.
The 2011 abstract specifies fused EcSTH and time-dependent metal effects. The graph retains abstract-only preparation limits and distinguishes its NADPH/thioNAD direction from2022.

text: In the 2004 MG1655 deletion/13C study, aerobic M9 cultures at37°C with5 g/L carbon source supported different physiological roles: PntAB supplied an estimated35–45% of biosynthetic NADPH during glucose growth, while loss of pntAB slowed growth and increased oxidative pentose-phosphate compensation. Soluble UdhA was important on acetate and in a pgi-deficient state with excess NADPH, rather than being required for ordinary glucose growth in that study. Some complementation results were described as data not shown. Crude-extract NADPH/APAD reverse assays measured enzyme capacity, not the same quantity as in-vivo redox flux.
independent_assessments: The 2004 deletion and carbon-balance analysis supports a condition-specific 35–45 percent anabolic contribution estimate. It is not a direct enzyme flux measurement or universal fraction.
The 2004 acetate/pgi phenotypes and reported plasmid rescue distinguish SthA's disposal role from PntAB supply. Rescue stated as data-not-shown is not presented as a displayed quantitative result.
The 2022 kinetic donor/acceptor pair is NADH/thioNADP; the 2004 extract capacity uses APAD. Neither surrogate is silently made natural NADP/NAD or a new native pathway substrate.

text: A 2004 redox-linked transcriptional interpretation was later tested more directly: the 2016 study found no correlation of transhydrogenase promoter activities with NADPH pools or formation/consumption fluxes across the tested perturbations. Paraquat at10 µM induced the zwf positive control without inducing pntAB or sthA. This narrows the earlier model under those conditions; it does not assert that every redox perturbation is transcriptionally inert.
independent_assessments: The 2016 reporter work challenges the earlier broad redox-pool transcription hypothesis. Both interpretations and their assay differences remain; neither creates a direct metabolite-binding edge.
The paraquat experiment includes zwf as a response comparator while the two transhydrogenase reporters do not rise at the tested dose. No global claim of oxidative-stress insensitivity is made.

text: The 2016 regulatory screen compared BW25113 with62 Keio transcription-factor deletions using low-copy whole-intergenic gfpmut2 reporters containing50–100 bp flanks. M9 cultures contained5 g/L glucose, glycerol or succinate at37°C; mid-exponential OD-normalized activity was taken over OD6000.7–1.5. All screen rows retain growth rates and deviations; most had two biological replicates and selected validations three. These are conditional expression responses. Below-threshold differences are not proof of absence, and a deletion response alone does not demonstrate direct promoter binding.
independent_assessments: Methods support BW25113/Keio, low-copy intergenic GFP reporters and specified growth/readout conditions. Endpoint qualifiers describe deletion-based inference, not direct promoter occupancy.
All supplementary screen conditions and 62 TF rows were read, including variation/growth columns. Failure to pass a threshold is not turned into an exhaustive negative biological claim.

text: IHF-alpha deletion reduced pntAB reporter activity to approximately0.15,0.16 and0.12 of wild type on succinate, glycerol and glucose, respectively. The IHF reference is an alpha/beta heterodimer; native component slots have no explicit coefficients, so the source descriptions are retained without inventing new component counts. Lrp deletion gave pntAB ratios0.43,0.42 and0.22 and sthA ratios1.43,1.68 and1.83 in the same carbon-source order; the main interpretation emphasized activation/repression on glycerol and glucose. ArgP activation of pntAB was identified on glucose and Fur activation on succinate. The proteins’ exact promoter-bound assemblies or metal states were not measured in this reporter study.
independent_assessments: The complete screen and main text support reduced pnt reporter after IHF-alpha deletion. The native alpha/beta complex bridge is explicit and a binding mechanism is not claimed.
The reporter ratios support conditional Lrp activation of pnt and repression of sth; amino-acid supplementation changes these effects. Separate 2019 native assertions do not replace these conditions.
ArgP/glucose and Fur/succinate effects are conditional reporter inferences. The record does not assume direct binding or a measured Fur metal state.

text: The aerobic 2016 ArcA-deletion experiment increased sthA expression on glucose, but did not detect ArcA activation of pntAB. This is distinct from the 2014 anaerobic MG1655 study: ArcA-8myc ChIP and ΔarcA expression comparisons in M9 with0.2% glucose and0.1% ammonium chloride, with or without20 mmol KNO3 at37°C, supported pntAB activation and sthA repression. Native PHOSPHO-ARCA remains the cited active state, mapped to reference ArcA with phosphoaspartate54. The original supplementary promoter-region peaks and occupancies are retained in the evidence ledger; modern coordinates are not substituted for that source genome version.
independent_assessments: Aerobic ArcA deletion raises sth expression but does not reproduce anaerobic pnt activation. The unmeasured phosphorylation state of this particular experiment is explicit.

Original 2014 ChIP and expression supplements support pnt activation and sth repression in anaerobic glucose with and without nitrate. Native phosphorylated ArcA and the ArcA-8myc/knockout preparations are distinguished.

text: With a20-amino-acid mixture, H-NS and CRP repressed the pntAB reporter; basal-medium results were different, including CRP-deletion glucose ratios0.53 for pntAB and0.57 for sthA and failure of that mutant to grow on glycerol or succinate. Supplementary mixture-condition pntAB activities were WT274.91±5.93, H-NS deletion630.91±16.85, CRP deletion499.85±29.74, IHF deletion139.95 and Lrp deletion319.20. TyrR deletion lowered sthA activity from WT801.20±167.35 to332.83±14.09 in this supplementary screen. This supports conditional expression effects, not a measured direct interaction or a universal sign.
independent_assessments: The amino-acid-mixture table supports H-NS/CRP repression under that condition, with different basal outcomes. Known cAMP-bound CRP is an inferred reference state, not measured promoter occupancy.
TableS4 supports the TyrR screen ratio under amino-acid mixture. Its evidentiary level is explicitly a supplementary expression observation, not validated direct binding or a universal sign.
All supplementary screen conditions and 62 TF rows were read, including variation/growth columns. Failure to pass a threshold is not turned into an exhaustive negative biological claim.

text: At5 mM single amino acid, leucine lowered pntAB and increased sthA reporter activity; lysine and histidine lowered pntAB, and methionine increased sthA. Valine prevented growth in that experiment and is not assigned an inhibitory promoter edge. Exact reference amino-acid charge forms identify the molecules without claiming that the medium contained an isolated ionic species. Exogenous cAMP reduced normalized pntAB activity by roughly50%, with only a marginal sthA decrease, after normalization to two constitutive reporters and verification of increased CRP activity. Native cAMP-bound CRP and the CRP dimer are represented, but the native component slots provide no ligand coefficient; direct pntA binding and occupancy were not measured.
independent_assessments: The single-amino-acid experiments support directional reporter responses at 5mM. Suggested Lrp/ArgP mediation is not promoted to direct ligand/protein or gene-binding evidence.
The cAMP experiment controls growth through two constitutive reporters and confirms CRP response. Extracellular cAMP lowering pnt expression is kept separate from general CRP activation.

text: The 2019 Lrp source used MG1655 ATCC47076 versus lrp::kan in MOPS0.2% glycerol,37°C,200 rpm, with MIN log OD6000.15–0.25 and transition OD6001.8–2.2. Native located assertions assign Lrp activation of pntA in log phase and phoA in transition, and repression of sthA in log phase. The full primary Methods were inspected, but the exact per-gene supplementary data were unavailable, so these target-level statements remain native curated assertions. The His-tagged Lrp used to generate antibody is not a tag on the cellular ChIP endpoint.
independent_assessments: The exact native 2019 regulation/target/phase joins support the three Lrp signs. Full primary Methods were read, but unavailable per-gene supplemental rows are not falsely claimed as directly inspected.

text: The 2017 Nac/CsiR study induced FLAG-tagged regulators from pT7-FLAG-4 in MG1655 in LB,1 mM IPTG for2 h from OD6000.2, with paired ChIP-seq and RNA-seq. Nac’s bound pntA row has peak1675942, coverage45, distance−15 and published normalized FC0.372191; this is not the raw4.3/13.24 ratio. Its cysQ row has peak4434633, coverage22, distance−145 and FC2.176844. Target assignment used the study’s proximity/operon framework, not promoter-specific site mutagenesis. Separate30°C nitrogen-depletion validation does not define these two rows or establish CysQ as the physiological NADP phosphatase.
independent_assessments: Fresh workbook row pntA gives peak1675942/coverage45/distance-15 and normalized FC0.372191. Raw coverage division is not substituted; proximity/operon assignment is weaker than target-site mutagenesis.

The fresh Nac workbook cysQ row supports the positive expression/binding join with exact normalized value. It adds conditional regulation, not evidence that CysQ is the physiological NADP phosphatase.

text: All16 selected-gene workbook rows are retained, including duplicate pntB operon annotations. CsiR, now called GlaR in the issuing reference, gave RNA-seq fold changes cysQ1.407187, nadK0.754291, phoA0.756034, pntA2.793539, pntB0.440537 and sthA0.587882; neither pntA nor pntB appeared in its bound-target sheet. Their opposite expression signs are preserved as potentially indirect responses. Corresponding Nac values were cysQ2.176844, nadK0.683302, phoA0.878483, pntA0.372191, pntB0.645038 and sthA0.879588. The ratios outside the bound Nac joins are quantitative context without invented statistical significance or blanket promoter-binding edges.
independent_assessments: Fresh CsiR RNA-seq row gives pntA FC2.793539, with no matching bound-target row in the complete bound sheet. The graph explicitly labels an indirect expression response.
All16 selected expression rows and duplicate pntB annotations were independently read. CsiR pntA and pntB have opposite signs, both expression-only; unreported significance is not invented.

text: Phosphorylated PhoB activates phoA through the exact native regulator→promoter PM00071→transcription-unit TU00052→phoA join. Its reference is P0AFJ5/phoB/b0399,229 residues, with phosphoaspartate53 and phosphorylation-dependent dimer orientation retained in the endpoint. P0A9I3 is GcvR and is explicitly rejected as PhoB. The 2013 acidic/aerobic versus microaerobic findings are available only through the primary abstract and native context, not full-body access. The 2019 phosphate-starvation reporter work used MG1655 promoter fragments, BCD2/msfgfp and pSEVA234/237 plasmids in DH10B resting cells at30°C over0–50 mM phosphate; synthetic Pliar constructs and modeled phosphorylation/feedback rates are separate from measured native-promoter outputs.
independent_assessments: The exact phosphorylated-PhoB/regulation/promoter/TU join identifies phoA. P0AFJ5, not rejected GcvR P0A9I3, is the correct issuing PhoB sequence and Asp53 state.
The 2019 phosphate work uses MG1655 promoter fragments in a DH10B plasmid reporter. Measured outputs, synthetic Pliar and model-derived feedback/phosphorylation remain distinct evidence levels.

text: Spot42 represses sthA in MG1655-derived strains. The 2011 Northern experiment used NM525 Δspf GS0433 with IPTG-induced pSpot42; the translational-fusion experiment used PM1205 Δspf GS0434 with pBAD sthA-lacZ from its TSS through9–15 codons,0.2% arabinose and ±1 mM IPTG for1 h. The table reports a−4.2±0.5 expression change. RegionIII mutation and compensatory target mutation support direct RNA pairing. The 2012 follow-up discusses multiple pairing regions, including I and III, without establishing simultaneous binding stoichiometry. Its nanC structural probing and Hfq-deletion experiments are not transferred to sthA; the sthA Hfq context in the earlier table retains that earlier source’s evidence level.
independent_assessments: The 2011 Northern/fusion experiments and compensatory mutations support Spot42-sth pairing. The two strain/construct systems are stated in prose because RNA is not a permitted protein endpoint qualifier.
The 2012 paper discusses multiple pairing regions but does not establish simultaneous stoichiometry. nanC probing/Hfq results are not misassigned as sth experiments.

text: Regulator reference annotations are retained separately from the pathway experiments. Lrp and ArgP have homodimer annotations; H-NS can form dimers and higher oligomers; TyrR changes between dimeric and tyrosine/ATP-associated higher assemblies. TyrR ATP binding enhances tyrosine affinity, but no particular TyrR assembly was measured at sthA. H-NS Lys121 hydroxyisobutyrylation, Fur His118 UMPylation, ArgP proteolysis, and GlaR glutarate relief of repression at glaH are known protein contexts, not demonstrated intermediates of the transhydrogenase reporter responses. Those unrelated target-specific mechanisms are not recursively imported as new pathway regulatory edges.
independent_assessments: The reporter ratios support conditional Lrp activation of pnt and repression of sth; amino-acid supplementation changes these effects. Separate 2019 native assertions do not replace these conditions.
ArgP/glucose and Fur/succinate effects are conditional reporter inferences. The record does not assume direct binding or a measured Fur metal state.
The amino-acid-mixture table supports H-NS/CRP repression under that condition, with different basal outcomes. Known cAMP-bound CRP is an inferred reference state, not measured promoter occupancy.
TableS4 supports the TyrR screen ratio under amino-acid mixture. Its evidentiary level is explicitly a supplementary expression observation, not validated direct binding or a universal sign.
Fresh CsiR RNA-seq row gives pntA FC2.793539, with no matching bound-target row in the complete bound sheet. The graph explicitly labels an indirect expression response.

text: The bounded iModulonDB check queried the six exact pathway loci and inspected ten selected module-member tables. None contained an exact target-locus match in that selection; alias/product substring matches were excluded. This is computational context and a bounded negative result, not global absence from iModulonDB or causal regulatory evidence. The Pseudomonas PathBank kinase/transhydrogenase definition with an unresolved protein and the archaeal phosphatases remain separate cross-source candidates, not organism-equivalent substitutes for the E. coli evidence.
independent_assessments: The original OWL contains two BiochemicalReaction instances plus one TransportWithBiochemicalReaction attached to the pathway. Counting only the first class was not the biological boundary; the final prose corrects it.
The archaeal enzymes and 85C assays are separate comparative contexts. The paper's starred/undetermined measurements are not transferred to E. coli.
Freshly hashed 25 API originals and all ten selected module tables contain no six-locus candidate members. This is a bounded computational screen, not global absence or mechanistic regulation.
